title: Probability II
description: The Statistics Department's second probability course: further permutations and combinations, probability laws and Bayes' rule, random variables, expectation, moments and Chebyshev's inequality, the discrete distributions (binomial, geometric, negative binomial, Poisson, hypergeometric), the continuous distributions (uniform, normal, exponential, gamma, chi-square), and joint, marginal and conditional distributions. Built from G. N. Amahia's STA 211 Probability II text (UI Distance Learning Centre), the updated lecture slides and the past papers from 2014 to 2024/25.

topics.title: Further Permutations and Combinations
topics.summary: Permutations count ordered arrangements and combinations unordered selections. STA 211 extends them to arrangements of alike objects, circular arrangements, selections with restrictions and the combinatorial identities used in proofs, such as Pascal's rule and Vandermonde's identity.

topics.title: Probability Laws, Conditional Probability and Bayes' Rule
topics.summary: Probability rests on three axioms. From them follow the complement and addition laws for two and three events. Conditional probability, independence, the total probability rule and Bayes' rule solve problems with partitions, such as which place a fisherman fished.
subtopics: Sample spaces, events and the axioms
The addition law for three events

topics.title: Random Variables, Expectation, Moments and Chebyshev's Inequality
topics.summary: A random variable has a probability mass or density function and a cumulative distribution function. Its expectation, variance and moments summarise the distribution, moment generating functions produce the moments, and Chebyshev's inequality bounds the probability of being far from the mean.

topics.title: Bernoulli, Binomial, Geometric and Negative Binomial Distributions
topics.summary: A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes. The binomial counts successes in n independent trials, the geometric counts the trials to the first success, and the negative binomial the trials to the kth success. Each has standard formulas for its probabilities, mean, variance and mgf.
subtopics: The binomial distribution and its properties
Mean, variance and mgf of the binomial

topics.title: The Poisson and Hypergeometric Distributions
topics.summary: The Poisson distribution models counts of rare events with mean λ, its mean and variance both equal λ, and it approximates the binomial when n is large and p small. The hypergeometric distribution models sampling without replacement from a finite population of two types.
subtopics: Mean, variance and mgf of the Poisson

topics.title: Uniform, Normal, Exponential, Gamma and Chi-square Distributions
topics.summary: Continuous distributions model measurements. The uniform distribution spreads probability evenly over an interval, the normal is the bell-shaped distribution standardised by z, the exponential models waiting times, and the gamma and chi-square families, with their moment generating functions, model sums of waiting times and squared normal variables.
subtopics: The gamma distribution and its mgf

topics.title: Joint, Marginal and Conditional Distributions
topics.summary: Two random variables have a joint distribution, from which marginal distributions are found by summing or integrating out the other variable, and conditional distributions by dividing by a marginal. Covariance measures linear association, independence factorises the joint density, and distributions of functions of random variables come from the CDF or transformation methods.
subtopics: Distributions of functions of random variables
